result.title: Resolution as Attention for Efficient Agent Memory Perception
result.summary: LLM-based agents accumulate extensive interaction histories when solving complex, long-horizon tasks, making efficient memory management critical to their performance and scalability. While existing memory management methods primarily focus on what to retain or retrieve, they often overlook how much perceptual detail should be allocated to individual past interactions. We posit that effective agent memory depends not only on the information preserved, but also on the granularity at which each past interaction is perceived. Motivated by this insight, we propose Resolution as Attention (RAA), a memory perception mechanism that uses visual resolution as a means of attention allocation across interaction histories. RAA renders past interactions as images and dynamically adjusts their resolution at every step according to their relevance to the agent's upcoming decision, preserving fine-grained information for critical interactions while reducing visual-token consumption for less relevant ones. To adaptively determine the perceptual fidelity of each interaction, we train a lightweight relevance estimator with teacher-model guidance and further optimize it to preserve the agent's decision consistency at a reduced visual-token cost. Experiments across multiple tasks and backbones show that RAA reduces token consumption by over 50% without compromising task performance. Moreover, RAA can be integrated as a plug-in perception layer with existing memory management methods, yielding further token savings and revealing adaptive perception as a complementary dimension of agent memory.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Resolution as Attention（RAA），把 agent 的过往交互渲染成图像，并按其对下一步决策的相关性动态调整分辨率，配合教师模型引导的轻量相关性估计器与决策一致性优化，在保持任务表现的同时将视觉 token 消耗降低一半以上。
AI.relevance_reason: 与「视觉细节应以何种粒度保留」及「按需获取视觉证据」的兴趣直接相关，分辨率即注意力可视作视觉证据筛选与感知预算分配的一种实现；但其作用于 agent 记忆而非推理期 latent 状态，与 LVR 中视觉旁路、信息坍缩的关系可供核查原文后判断。
